title: BME (CDRI-08) mitigates hypoxia-induced hippocampal neurodegeneration and memory impairment via modulating NMDAR-CREB-BDNF signaling and apoptosis reduction
task: Mitigate hypoxia-induced hippocampal neurodegeneration and memory impairment
key_results: BME restored NR2A/NR2B expression, reversed CREB-BDNF suppression, increased pyramidal neuron spine density, and reduced cleaved caspase-3 and pro-apoptotic proteins (BAD, BAX) while elevating Bcl-2
comments: The study effectively demonstrates multi-target intervention via natural extract, though causality between individual signaling nodes and memory recovery could be more precisely established through targeted knockdown approaches.

outputs: apoptotic markers (cleaved caspase-3, BAD, BAX, Bcl-2, Cyt C)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Extra-synaptic NMDAR activation (GluN2B upregulation, NR2A downregulation) combined with PSD-95 loss triggers apoptotic cascades under hypoxia
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; BME restored NR2A/NR2B balance and reduced apoptosis

hypotheses.hypothesis: CREB-BDNF suppression contributes to synaptic dysfunction and memory deficits in hypoxia
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; BME reversed CREB-BDNF suppression and restored memory performance

hypotheses.hypothesis: BME increases neuronal plasticity and reduces apoptosis via modulation of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; BME increased spine density and Bcl-2 while decreasing caspase-3, BAD, BAX
